name: Food Not Bombs Raleigh
description: Volunteer collective sharing free vegan meals, groceries, toiletries and often clothing downtown. Also takes requests for grocery and diaper deliveries.
address: Moore Square, 201 S Blount St, Raleigh, NC 27601
access: Anyone; no ID, no sign-up
notes: Saturday sharing is at the Martin St side across from Moore Square, around 4 E Martin St. In extreme weather it may run only 3–4 pm, and it ends early when food runs out. Clothing usually goes in the first hour. Contact: fnbraleigh@gmail.com, or text the number above.

name: Raleigh United Mutual Aid Hub (RUMAH)
description: Volunteer-run, community-funded social center (since 2023). Collects and distributes donations for local groups and hosts free community dinners, clothing swaps, mending circles, workshops, a community garden and a coworking space. Keeps a public Triangle resource directory.
access: Open to all; sober space
notes: The site says 'We're moving! We'll have a new location in late 2026,' so check the site or Instagram (@raleighunitedmutualaidhub) for the current address. Address is from its Visit Raleigh listing. Email: contact.rumah@gmail.com.

name: Raleigh Really Really Free Market
description: Monthly free market where nothing is bought or sold: bring what you can, take what you need. Skill shares too (past markets had free haircuts and bike-repair lessons).
address: Eliza Pool Park, 1600 Fayetteville St, Raleigh, NC 27603
hours: 2nd Sunday of each month, 11 am–1 pm (rain date: following Sunday)
access: No sign-up needed, just show up
notes: Upcoming dates listed on its site: Nov 8 and Dec 13, 2026. Masks encouraged and provided. Please take unclaimed items home. Instagram: @raleighrrfm_; email raleighrrfm0@gmail.com.

name: Raleigh Community Kickstand
description: All-volunteer community bike co-op (since 2017). Free bike repairs and maintenance lessons, and gives away refurbished bikes, with a focus on people facing housing insecurity.
address: Oak City Cares, 1430 S Wilmington St, Raleigh, NC 27603
hours: Monthly repair and bike giveaway: 2nd Saturday, 1–3 pm
access: Walk up; first come, first served
notes: Also runs pop-up repair events around Raleigh (see calendar on site) and community shop hours at its storage space. Email volunteer@raleighcommunitykickstand.org for the gate code. General contact: info@raleighcommunitykickstand.org.

name: Triangle Tenant Union
description: Member-run tenant union, part of the NC Tenants Union, covering Raleigh, Durham and Chapel Hill. Helps tenants form associations in their buildings and neighborhoods to fight rent hikes, displacement and unsafe conditions.
access: Any tenant; join through the website
notes: This is organizing, not a service agency, and members pay dues. Email: triangletenantunion@gmail.com; Instagram: @triangletenants.

name: Oak City Cares
description: Multi-service center for people at risk of or experiencing homelessness. Free showers and laundry on weekdays, three meals a day on weekends and holidays, care coordinators, public computers, phones and lockable phone charging, plus an on-site clinic and HIV/STD/Hep C testing. Coordinated Entry access site for shelter referrals.
hours: Mon–Fri 9 am–5 pm (last shower 4:30, last laundry 3:30); Sat, Sun and holidays meals at 9 am, 12:30 pm and 3 pm
access: Walk-in; no appointment; no fees
notes: GoRaleigh route 21 from downtown. Care Coordinators see people Mon–Fri 9 am–3 pm (until 1 pm on Wednesdays). Shelter referrals are in person only. Amplify Health (formerly Advance Community Health) runs walk-in primary care here Mon, Tue and Thu 9 am–1 pm.

name: Women's Center of Wake County – Day Shelter
description: Day shelter for single women experiencing homelessness. Breakfast and lunch, showers, laundry, hygiene supplies, a clothing closet, day storage, computers, phones and help getting IDs and other documents, plus on-site health care and housing navigators.
hours: Day shelter intake 8–11 am; breakfast 8:30–9:30 am; lunch 11:30 am–12:30 pm
access: Unaccompanied women; same-day intake
notes: Its Recuperative Respite program for women leaving the hospital is by referral, at 2200 New Bern Ave.

name: Wake County Drop-In Overnight Shelter (Second Street Place / temporary Bramer Dr site)
description: Wake County's low-barrier emergency shelter for men and women. No referral is needed for emergency access, and it doesn't require sobriety or background checks.
hours: Temporary site: 7 pm–7 am (overnight intake 6–8 pm)
access: Walk-in; adults experiencing homelessness
notes: Second Street Place (5010 Second St, Raleigh 27609, normally 24/7) closed for renovation in 2026, and the county expects to reopen it in late 2026. Until then, the Women's Center runs the drop-in shelter at 3211 Bramer Dr (hours are from wcwc.org/gethelp). Call 211 to check which site is open.

name: South Wilmington Street Center (men's shelter)
description: Wake County shelter for men experiencing homelessness. Short-term emergency overnight dorms, plus longer-term beds for men working with case management, budgeting help and mental health and substance use referrals.
access: Adult men; call about bed availability
notes: A May 2025 local resource guide lists it as for Wake County residents only. The county page doesn't state requirements, so confirm by phone.

name: Healing Transitions
description: Recovery community with an emergency drop-in shelter and non-medical detox. Serves people 'under the influence or not, and regardless of readiness for change.'
address: 1251 Goode St, Raleigh, NC 27603 (men); 3304 Glen Royal Rd, Raleigh, NC 27617 (women)
access: Adults; call first (see notes)
notes: Local guides from 2023–2025 say to call ahead to be screened or considered for the night, and the process differs for men and women. Wake County lists detox lines: men ext. 135, women ext. 222.

name: Wrenn House (Haven House youth shelter)
description: Crisis line and emergency shelter for youth who have run away, are unhoused, or are in crisis.
access: Youth (a 2025 guide lists ages 10–17; a guardian must start screening)
notes: You can also text SAFE to 4HELP (44357). Call for intake.

name: Urban Ministries of Wake County – Food Pantry
description: Weekly curbside grocery box with produce (much of it from on-site community gardens), meat, eggs and pantry staples.
hours: Mon–Thu from 8:30 am until capacity is reached
access: Any Wake County resident; no referral needed
notes: One box per household per week. The 919-746-0088 info line has closings and news. The July 2026 Food Shuttle guide says to show ID and arrive early.

name: Shepherd's Table Soup Kitchen
description: Free, no-questions-asked hot lunch on weekdays.
access: No referral required
notes: It's in the basement of the Church of the Good Shepherd, entered from the back at Morgan and McDowell Sts. Address and phone are from a May 2025 local resource guide.

name: Catholic Parish Outreach Food Pantry
description: Large walk-in food pantry run by Catholic Charities of the Diocese of Raleigh. No religious participation is required.
hours: Mon, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat 9 am–noon
access: No referral or ID needed (2025 guide); residents of Wake, Johnston or Franklin counties
notes: Food once a month, served indoors. Spanish line: (919) 873-0094. The 'no referral or ID' detail is from the May 2025 local resource guide (rhanc.gov).

name: Wake Relief Food Pantry
description: Downtown indoor food pantry.
address: 4 N Blount St, 1st Floor, Raleigh, NC 27601
hours: Mon & Tue 1–3 pm; Wed 10 am–noon; 4th Saturday 10 am–noon
access: Wake County residents
notes: Food once every 30 days.

name: Lincoln Park Holiness Church Food Pantry
description: Walk-up window food pantry in Southeast Raleigh.
access: Short intake process; walk up to the window
notes: The source lists no ID or religious requirement. Confirm by phone.

name: Open Door Clinic (Urban Ministries of Wake County)
description: Free medical home for uninsured adults: primary care, behavioral health, some specialty care, diabetes education, telehealth and an on-site pharmacy.
hours: Mon & Thu 9 am–5 pm; Tue & Wed 9 am–6:30 pm; Fri closed. Pharmacy Mon–Thu 10 am–noon and 1–4 pm
access: Uninsured adults
notes: Spanish line: (919) 746-0102. A May 2025 guide adds: 18+, not Medicaid-eligible, and not pregnant (no prenatal care). No urgent care or dental. Call about becoming a new patient.

name: NC Harm Reduction Coalition – Raleigh
description: Free naloxone (Narcan) kits and syringe services, prioritizing people who use drugs and their families. Mobile and peer exchange is available by call or text.
access: No ID; call or text before visiting
notes: NCHRC says staff are mostly in the field, so call or text first. Its contact page lists its main office at 4024 Barrett Dr, Suite 101.

name: Wake County Public Health Pharmacy – Free Naloxone
description: Free naloxone kits from the county pharmacy while supplies last.
notes: The county also has naloxone vending machines at SouthLight (2101 Garner Rd) and the Wake County Detention Center (3301 Hammond Rd), and newspaper boxes with naloxone around the county through Illuminate NC.

name: SouthLight Peer Drop-In Center – Naloxone Vending Machine
description: Free naloxone vending machine inside SouthLight Healthcare's peer drop-in center.
notes: Hours aren't listed on the county page.

name: Amplify Health – Southeast Raleigh Careplex (formerly Advance Community Health)
description: Federally funded community health center with primary care, behavioral health and pharmacy. Also runs an urgent care at 3509 Capital Blvd (Mon–Sat 8 am–5 pm).
hours: Mon–Thu 7 am–7 pm; Fri 7 am–5 pm
access: Insured and uninsured patients
notes: It rebranded from Advance Community Health; the old advancechc.org redirects. The site says it is a federal Health Center Program grantee (these offer income-based sliding fees), but I didn't see its sliding-fee details. Confirm when you call.

name: Wake Recovery Response Center (WakeBrook campus)
description: Behavioral health urgent care and crisis center for adults in a mental health or substance use crisis, run by RI International (Recovery Innovations). 'No wrong door': walk in alone, with a loved one, or be brought by a provider or first responder.
access: Adults 18+; walk-ins accepted
notes: Cost and hours aren't stated on the county pages. A 2024 county FAQ described it as 24/7. Also see the WakeBrook campus page on wake.gov.

name: Monarch Behavioral Health Urgent Care
description: Walk-in behavioral health urgent care for mental health and substance use needs, ages 4 and up.
hours: Mon–Thu 8 am–10 pm; Fri 8 am–8 pm; Sat–Sun 8 am–5 pm
access: Walk-in; ages 4+
notes: Cost isn't stated on the county page. Ask about fees and insurance.

name: Therapeutic Alternatives Mobile Crisis (Wake)
description: Mobile crisis team that sends a mental health professional to you instead of EMS or police.
access: Call anytime
notes: Wake County also lists the Alliance Health crisis line (877-223-4617) and 988 (call or text; text AYUDA for Spanish).

name: InterAct of Wake County
description: Domestic violence and sexual assault services: 24-hour crisis line, emergency shelter, the Solace Center (24/7 sexual assault forensic exams), court advocacy for protective orders, counseling and housing case management.
hours: Crisis line 24/7; walk-in Mon–Fri 9 am–5 pm
access: Confidential; walk-ins welcome during office hours
notes: Spanish line: 844-203-8896. Email gethelp@interactofwake.org (answered weekdays). Solace Center services are free whatever the circumstances.

name: Legal Aid of North Carolina – Raleigh Office
description: Free civil legal help for low-income people, including housing and eviction, domestic violence, consumer, public benefits and health care issues.
address: 1425 Promise Beacon Circle, Suite 201, Raleigh, NC 27610
access: Income-eligible residents of Wake and Johnston counties
notes: Statewide intake helpline: 1-866-219-5262 (Mon–Fri 8:30 am–4 pm).

name: El Centro Hispano – Raleigh Office
description: Latino-led community organization offering legal information and referrals, Know Your Rights workshops, community assistance and education and workforce programs.
access: Spanish and English
notes: The 2024 brochure lists 'Immigration and Legal Assistance' among its programs. Call to confirm current services and hours.

name: LGBT Center of Raleigh – Community Closet & Pantry
description: Free Community Closet with everyday clothing, shoes and gender-affirming items (binders, makeup and wigs on request), plus a Community Pantry with shelf-stable food. Also a drop-in community center.
hours: Wed & Thu noon–6 pm; Fri noon–4 pm; Sat 11 am–2 pm
access: Drop in during open hours
notes: Hours can change around programs and holidays, so check the center's calendar.

name: Diaper Train
description: Diaper bank serving only Wake County. Free diapers and youth and adult incontinence supplies.
hours: Tue 9 am–noon; Wed 3–5:30 pm; Thu 9 am–noon; 2nd Saturday 9 am–noon
access: Needs an online referral from a community partner (e.g. Wake County social workers, schools, pediatricians); proof of Wake County residency
notes: Once every four weeks. If you can't get a referral, Food Not Bombs Raleigh takes diaper delivery requests through its Linktree.

name: Raleigh Tool Share
description: City program that lends battery-powered yard tools (mower, string trimmer, leaf blower) for free.
address: Raleigh Pathways Center, 900 S Wilmington St, Raleigh, NC 27601
hours: Pickup Wed or Fri 9 am–noon; return the following Monday 9 am–noon
access: Raleigh city-limits residents; NC ID and proof of residency; online request form
notes: Non-commercial use only. You sign a liability release at pickup. Not low-barrier: needs ID and an address.

name: Wake County Human Services (Swinburne)
description: County office for food and nutrition benefits (SNAP), Medicaid, emergency assistance, child welfare, and veteran and homeless services. NCWorks Career Center is in the same building.
notes: Listed in the May 2025 local resource guide. Call for current lobby hours.

name: NC 211 (United Way)
description: Free 24-hour information and referral line for shelter, food, utilities and other help, including White Flag shelter info.
access: Anyone; phone call
notes: The May 2025 guide also lists 1-800-831-1754. Wake County's crisis page says to dial 211.

name: Wake County Public Libraries – free card services
description: 23 free public libraries across Wake County. Cardholders can borrow laptops, Wi-Fi hotspots and blood pressure monitors, get free online tutoring (Tutor.com) and Udemy courses, book one-on-one job-search and tech help, and take seeds from seed libraries at some branches.
access: Library card is free for Wake County residents
notes: The card page doesn't say how people without a permanent address can register, so ask at a branch. The system has a mobile library card option and new STEAM Labs.

name: Cary Really Really Free Market
description: Monthly free market where nothing is bought or sold. Bring what you can, take what you need.
address: Walnut Street Park, 1420 Walnut St, Cary, NC
access: Open to all
notes: From Triangle on the Cheap's free-markets roundup (updated Sept 2026). I couldn't find an organizer page, so check before going.

name: NeighborUp – Cary (formerly Dorcas Ministries)
description: Client-choice food pantry (nonperishables, frozen meat, produce, dairy), emergency financial help with housing and bills, free career coaching, and the low-cost Dorcas Thrift Shop.
access: Residents of Cary, Morrisville, Apex, Holly Springs, Fuquay-Varina, Willow Spring, New Hill or Friendship, or a child in public school there, or unhoused with a last address there
notes: Food once every 30 days. The campus is at 187 High House Rd. The thrift shop sells items and isn't free.

name: Mariam Clinic
description: Free volunteer clinic for uninsured, low-income adults: acute and chronic care, women's health, mental health and psychiatry, free labs, eye exams and dental referrals. Interpreters for Arabic, Hindi, Urdu and Bengali.
address: 1100 NW Maynard Rd, Suite 110, Cary, NC 27513
hours: Sundays 11 am–5 pm, by appointment only
access: Adults 18+, uninsured, at or below 200% of the federal poverty level; no walk-ins
notes: No emergency, walk-in or prenatal care.

name: NeighborUp – Apex (formerly Western Wake Crisis Ministry)
description: Client-choice food pantry and emergency financial help with housing and bills for western Wake County.
address: 1600 Olive Chapel Rd, Suite 408, Apex, NC 27502
access: Residents of Cary, Morrisville, Apex, Holly Springs, Fuquay-Varina, Willow Spring, New Hill or Friendship, or unhoused with a last address there
notes: Food once every 30 days.

name: Amplify Health – Apex
description: Federally funded community health center (formerly Advance Community Health) with primary care.
notes: See the Southeast Raleigh entry for the note on sliding fees. Confirm by phone.

name: Morrisville Community Library
description: Free Wake County public library branch with a warm indoor space. Cardholders can borrow laptops and Wi-Fi hotspots and get free tutoring and job-search help (see the countywide library entry).
access: Open to the public; free card for Wake residents

name: Garner Area Ministries
description: Long-running local nonprofit (since 1981) offering emergency help with rent, water bills and prescriptions, plus a thrift shop.
hours: Assistance office Mon, Wed & Fri 9 am–noon
access: Garner residents (zip 27529 and parts of 27603 and 27610)
notes: The thrift shop at 560–564 Village Ct (919-772-9178; Mon/Wed/Sat 9 am–1 pm, Fri 9 am–3 pm) sells items and isn't free. Office hours are from GAM's website (checked Nov 2026); eligibility is from the May 2025 guide. GAM's site says pantry food is available once every three months, with emergency food any time.

name: Community of Hope Ministries Food Pantry
description: Church food pantry with weekday indoor hours and a monthly evening drive-through.
hours: Tue & Thu 11 am–noon; 1st Thu 5:30–7 pm (drive-through); 3rd Thu 6–7 pm (indoor)
access: ID required for every family member
notes: Food up to twice a month. Not low-barrier because of the ID requirement. Each family receives counseling before picking food; the site describes a Christian ministry but doesn't say whether the counseling is religious or optional.

name: Tri-Area Ministry Food Pantry
description: Drive-through food pantry for the Wake Forest / Rolesville / Youngsville area.
address: 149 E Holding Ave, Wake Forest, NC 27587
hours: Mon & Wed 10 am–1 pm; 2nd and 3rd Saturday 10 am–1 pm
access: Drive-through
notes: Food once a month. The source lists no religious requirement.

name: Richland Creek Community Church Food Pantry
description: Indoor food distribution twice a month.
address: 3229 Burlington Mills Rd, Wake Forest, NC 27587
access: Arrive early
notes: The source lists no religious requirement.

name: Amplify Health – Wake Forest
description: Federally funded community health center (formerly Advance Community Health) with primary care.
notes: See the Southeast Raleigh entry for the note on sliding fees.

name: CrossPoint Community Church Mobile Food Distribution
description: Monthly drive-through food distribution.
access: Drive-through
notes: Listed as Cross Point Community Church in Inter-Faith Food Shuttle's Oct 2026 food resources guide.

name: East Regional Library
description: Free Wake County public library branch serving eastern Wake. Cardholders can borrow laptops and hotspots and get free tutoring and job-search help (see the countywide library entry).
access: Open to the public; free card for Wake residents

name: Fuquay-Varina Emergency Food Pantry
description: Drive-through emergency food pantry. Also connects patrons with financial-assistance and clothing resources.
access: Drive-through; clear your trunk or back seat
notes: Once every 28 days. Hours are from the Harnett County DSS pantry list updated 1/21/2026. Income-based eligibility; bring photo ID and proof of address. Drive-through.

name: Operation Nahyelle
description: Curbside food distribution in downtown Fuquay-Varina.
hours: 1st and 3rd Saturday 10 am–noon; 2nd and 4th Thursday 3:30–5:30 pm
access: Curbside

name: Amplify Health – Fuquay-Varina
description: Federally funded community health center (formerly Advance Community Health) with primary care.
address: 130 N Judd Pkwy NE, Fuquay-Varina, NC 27526
notes: See the Southeast Raleigh entry for the note on sliding fees.

name: Holly Springs Food Cupboard
description: Local food pantry with a weekly drive-through.
address: 621 W Holly Springs Rd, Holly Springs, NC 27540
access: Book Monday visits in advance; empty your trunk for the drive-through
notes: An older county list says food once every 30 days. Hours are from the Harnett County DSS list updated 1/21/2026.

name: Wendell Community Library
description: Free Wake County public library branch. Cardholders can borrow laptops and hotspots and get free tutoring and job-search help (see the countywide library entry).
access: Open to the public; free card for Wake residents

name: Shepherd's Care Medical Clinic
description: Free rural clinic for uninsured adults in eastern Wake and nearby counties. Also runs a monthly drive-through food distribution.
hours: Food distribution: 3rd Wednesday of each month, 1 pm (drive-through)
access: Uninsured adults (clinic); drive-through (food)
notes: The food schedule is from the July 2026 Food Shuttle guide. Clinic details (primary care, behavioral health, free) are from older directory listings. Call to check clinic hours and whether it's taking new patients.

name: Bread for Life of America – Zebulon Distribution
description: Monthly drive-through food distribution at the Boys and Girls Club.
access: Drive-through

notes: Run by Raleigh Dream Center, a Christian ministry. Groceries are free. Volunteers may offer to pray with you or talk about faith, but nothing we found says you have to take part. Call (919) 867-4446 to confirm days and times.
description: Mobile food pantry run by Raleigh Dream Center: free groceries handed out at this neighborhood stop.
name: Parrish Manor – Raleigh Dream Center mobile pantry
hours: Every other Tuesday at 11:30 am, until supplies run out
